title: Tetzaveh: Moses' name is missing
hookLine: Moses isn't named in this portion; some link it to his offer to be blotted out for his people (Exodus 32:32)

cards: Look closely at the credits of a big movie and you'll find hundreds of names. But the person who stayed up all night fixing the sound in one scene might not be there.

The neighbor who watched the director's kids for a year definitely isn't. Since the night he was born in Egypt, Moses has been in almost every scene of the Torah: Pharaoh, the bush, the plagues, the sea, Sinai.
Then comes this portion, Tetzaveh. Read it start to finish, and his name isn't in it once.

teach.b: People who read the Torah closely have long pointed this out. From his birth in Exodus to the end of Numbers, Tetzaveh is said to be the one weekly portion where the name Moses never appears. He isn't absent, though.
The portion opens, in Hebrew, v'atah tetzaveh: and you, you shall command. God is speaking to Moses the whole time. Make the oil.

teach.h: V'ATAH: AND YOU, ON EVERY LINE.
teach.b: Moses is the you on every line, everywhere and unnamed. Why? The Torah doesn't say.
A medieval commentator, the Baal HaTurim, looks ahead a few chapters, to the golden calf.

teach.h: BLOT ME OUT OF THY BOOK.
teach.b: After the people sin, Moses pleads for them, and says to God, in the old Jewish translation: "blot me, I pray Thee, out of Thy book which Thou hast written." Forgive them, or take my name out.
The Baal HaTurim says the words of a righteous person carry weight even when said conditionally, and so his name was left out of one portion.
Others notice that this portion is all about Aaron, his brother: Aaron's clothes, Aaron's sons, Aaron's role.
Perhaps Moses steps back so his brother can stand in the light. Neither answer is in the text itself, but both point the same way.
The greatest prophet in the Torah spends a whole portion as the unnamed you, doing the work, giving instructions that make someone else shine.

how: Jewish teachers often point out Moses' missing name when Tetzaveh is read; tradition also places Moses' death on the seventh of Adar, which often falls near this portion. Jewish law ranks giving anonymously among the highest forms of tzedakah.

s: Moses is absent from the events of Tetzaveh
he's there the whole time, as the you God speaks to; only his name is missing.
the Torah explains why his name is left out
it doesn't. the Baal HaTurim and others offer readings.
Moses once asked to be blotted out of God's book for his people
after the golden calf: forgive them, or blot me out.

games.q: the people have sinned. you're Moses, pleading with God. what do you say?
o: forgive them, or blot me out of Thy book.
start over with a new people.
games.why: blot me out of Thy book. the Baal HaTurim says that's why one portion carries no name of Moses.

practice: Think of something kind you could do where no one would know it was you: paying for someone's coffee, praising a colleague to their boss out of their hearing, giving anonymously. Picture doing it and walking away without a word.
If part of you wants credit, that's normal; let it be there, and stay with the picture anyway.
